liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Stella Blue** (2 reviews): The lead-in to Stella Blue quotes Joy of Man's Desiring for roughly thirty seconds; Reviewer calls Stella Blue excellent, and disputes that the second set was lackluster [20][30]
- **Sugaree** (1 review): Sugaree is named as one of the strong tracks worth keeping [22]
- **Peggy-O** (1 review): Reviewer recommends Peggy-O as one of the standout performances of the night [21]
- **Althea** (1 review): Althea is also named as a strong track worth burning [22]
- **Passenger** (1 review): Reviewer singles out Passenger as worth hearing [21]
- **China Cat Sunflower** (1 review): The China Cat into Rider sequence was this attendee's highlight of an uneven show [24]
- **Alabama Getaway** (1 review): When the second set opened with Alabama Getaway, the attendee sensed it would be a standard set [24]
- **Bertha** (1 review): Bertha features Jerry's upbeat double-picking, more energetic than he had played in a while [30]

## Setlist highlights

- **Brahms Tease**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [31]

## The recordings

- **gd81-03-14.aud.hayum.7217.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): audience recording; 24 songs; 168 min; rated 4.5/5 by 12 [1]. Said about its sound: Decent recording with a good mix; Jerry's guitar stands out clearly; The mix was great in the hall, and the taper's setup still sounds great decades later [22][24]
- **gd1981-03-14.nak700.glassberg.motb.84826.sbeok.flac16**: source not stated; 24 songs; 167 min; rated 4.51/5 by 55 [4]
- **gd1981-03-14.174928.aud.Bernstein.ackerman.noel.flac2496**: audience recording; 22 songs; 161 min [6]. Said about its sound: The taper was positioned centrally and close to the stage; tape flips were crossfaded where applicable [6]
- **gd1981-03-14.nak700.rolfe.miller.95288.flac24**: source not stated; 23 songs; 167 min; rated 1.67/5 by 3 [7]
- **gd1981-03-14.157926.fob.nak700.cm.wagner.miller.t.flac1644**: source not stated; 22 songs; 169 min [10]

## Around the show

- Reviewer hitched down from Keene State College after a party the night before, attending with a Connecticut friend; it was their last Dead show [19]
- Final show before the band's spring 1981 European tour; an energetic crowd, with dynamics swinging between very loud and very quiet [21]
- Reviewer had also seen the band at the Garden and in Boston; here the first set was strong but the second lost energy [23]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd81-03-14.aud.hayum.7217.sbeok.shnf**: source: Audience Recording [1]. Also: Audience source of uncertain origin, taken from CD through EAC to SHN, circulated via Andy Hayum [1]
- **gd1981-03-14.nak700.glassberg.motb.84826.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Barry Glassberg; transferred by A. Egert and C. Ladner; source: Nakamichi CM700's > Sony TC-D5M > MAC [4]. Also: Source is Barry Glassberg's spring 1981 Nakamichi recording, transferred by the MOTB team; MOTB stands for Mouth Of The Beast, the taping spot front and center between stage and soundboard [25][27]
- **gd1981-03-14.174928.aud.Bernstein.ackerman.noel.flac2496**: taped by Master Cassettes Recorded by Jon Bernstein; transferred by Transfer by Ray Ackerman Edited & Mastered by Joe Noel October 26, 2025; source: ?? mics > ?? lead deck > ?? Deck > Master Cassettes [6]
- **gd1981-03-14.nak700.rolfe.miller.95288.flac24**: taped by Steve Rolfe; transferred by Charlie Miller; source: (FOB) Nakamichi 700 -> Cassette Master (Sony D5/Maxell UDXL-IIS) [7]. Also: Front-of-board Nakamichi 700 cassette master, with masters lent by Steve Rolfe; a CD version came from unknown mics [7]
- **gd1981-03-14.157926.fob.nak700.cm.wagner.miller.t.flac1644**: taped by Bob Wagner; transferred by All Transfers and Mastering by Charlie Miller  August 24, 2022; source: (FOB/8th Row) Nakamichi CM700 > Cassette Master (Sony TC-D5M/Maxell UDXL-IIS) [10]. Also: Bob Wagner's masters were used; Barry Glassberg operated Wagner's deck, and Steve Rolfe supplied the patch source [10]
